solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Confined after fall, son certain to drink given the circumstances (9)

indicatorNotes.to drink: S and BOUND take NOW inside, as a drinker takes in a drink

blocks.note: now = as things stand, 'now that you mention it'

annotation.surface: Someone is laid up after a tumble, and their son is sure to hit the bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'fall' is not a tumble but a snowfall, and being snowbound is exactly being confined after one.
annotation.definitionFit: Snowbound means stuck indoors because snow has fallen.

entries.clue: Excessively demanding way to go up (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' means read the piece from bottom to top

blocks.note: go = PEE (to go to the loo), turned upward

annotation.surface: A hard climb, described as a demanding path uphill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go' in its toilet sense is PEE; the whole tail reads like a hill path, which is why 'way to go up' hides so well.
annotation.definitionFit: A steep price or demand is an excessive one.

entries.clue: Poem on ailing and death got English disturbed (3,2,1,11)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: the letters are stirred up into a new order

annotation.surface: A reviewer complains that a poem about illness and death left the English upset.
annotation.walkthrough: Fitting, since Keats's ode is itself steeped in sickness and death ('where youth grows pale, and spectre-thin, and dies').
annotation.definitionFit: Keats's Ode to a Nightingale is one of the best-known English poems.

entries.clue: Tour vehicles club employs to take band to the north (11)

indicatorNotes.to the north: in a down clue, heading north means reading upward

annotation.surface: A club hires a coach to take its band north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like musicians on tour with the club; it is a belt. A battle bus is the coach a party leader tours in during a British election campaign.
annotation.definitionFit: Battle buses are the campaign coaches politicians tour the country in.

entries.clue: Jock’s awful problem heard by judge periodically (6)

indicatorNotes.heard: use the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a sum is a maths problem

annotation.surface: A Scotsman laments a dreadful difficulty brought before a judge now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jock' is the crossword's Scotsman, flagging a Scots word: ugsome means horrible or loathsome.
annotation.definitionFit: Ugsome is Scots for horrible or disgusting.

entries.clue: Perish eating faceless Italian food’s enzyme (8)

indicatorNotes.eating: DIE takes the next piece inside it
indicatorNotes.faceless: lose the first letter, the face

annotation.surface: A threat to die rather than eat stale pasta, or a warning about its enzymes.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'S from 'food's' is part of the wordplay, not just grammar.
annotation.definitionFit: Diastase is the enzyme that breaks starch down into sugar.

entries.clue: Managed one day going round capital of Jordan (5)

indicatorNotes.going round: turn the letters about, reading right to left

annotation.surface: A visitor squeezed a tour of Amman into a single day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Jordan' begs for AMMAN or a J; capital here is money, and the dinar is Jordan's currency.
annotation.definitionFit: The dinar is Jordan's currency, and capital means money.

entries.clue: Filmmaker might do this disruptive occupation, perhaps (6,6)

blocks.note: a film director may direct an action film
protesters occupying a building, a sit-in; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a wider kind of protest

annotation.surface: A film crew takes over a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' looks like a job, which fits the filmmaker; it is the protesters' occupying of a building.
annotation.definitionFit: Occupying a building is a classic form of direct action protest.

entries.clue: Fresh enthusiasm over contents of sandy Pacific islands (3,7)

indicatorNotes.contents of: take the inside letters of the word that follows

annotation.surface: A traveller is newly keen on sandy South Sea islands.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' just stacks the first pieces above the last.
annotation.definitionFit: A country named by its geography: the nation is two main islands and many small ones in the south-west Pacific.

entries.clue: Regret admitting sporting gaffe’s not an honest one (5)

indicatorNotes.admitting: RUE lets the next piece in

blocks.note: OG = own goal, the footballer's blunder

annotation.surface: A footballer admits an own goal but says it wasn't a cheat's.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's after 'gaffe' reads as 'is', leading into the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym given as a description: a rogue is a scoundrel, the opposite of an honest man.

entries.clue: Investigate South American money, but only a little before time (4,3)

blocks.note: a sou was a tiny French coin, 'not a sou'

annotation.surface: Look into South American money, but only briefly before the clock runs out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one region; it splits into S and US. Suss out is British slang for working something out.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: to suss something out is to look into it until you understand it.

entries.clue: Pace around Bologna at intervals with loud baby (5-4)

indicatorNotes.around: SPEED goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.at intervals: things that come at intervals come with gaps between, so read a letter, skip one, read the next

annotation.surface: Someone paces round Bologna with a noisy infant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Baby' is a verb: to baby someone is to pamper them, as spoon-feeding does.
annotation.definitionFit: To spoon-feed is to baby someone, doing everything for them.

entries.clue: Item from dairy best available after switching locations (6,5)

annotation.surface: A dairy's finest product is on sale once it has been moved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best available' reads as a single phrase; it is two words to be written the other way round. Single cream is the thinner British pouring cream.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this thin pouring cream is one of the things a dairy sells.

entries.clue: Arab soon to return (5)

indicatorNotes.to return: the phrase comes back the other way

annotation.surface: An Arab will be back shortly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a mo' is British shorthand for 'in a moment'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: people from Oman, on the Arabian Peninsula, are Arabs.

entries.clue: Coloured garment fastened with last bits of sticky tape (3-3)

indicatorNotes.last bits of: take the final letter of each word

annotation.surface: A coloured garment held together with sticky tape.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bodged repair; tie-dyeing is done by tying cloth before dyeing it.
annotation.definitionFit: The name of the technique stands for the shirt it produces, knotted before dyeing so the colour comes out in swirls.

entries.clue: Force out unsatisfactory individual, becoming leaderless (5)

indicatorNotes.becoming leaderless: a word's leader is its first letter, so a word left without a leader has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: REJECT, a person turned down, without its R

annotation.surface: An unwanted member is pushed out and the group loses its head.
annotation.walkthrough: A reject is someone or something not good enough.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bouncers eject troublemakers, forcing them out of the door.

entries.clue: Singer chats about simple arrangement (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'about turn', the soldier's order to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a row is the simplest arrangement, things in a line

annotation.surface: A vocalist talks about a stripped-back version of a song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: 'singer' is a stock disguise for any songbird, and the sparrow is one.

entries.clue: Scraped together mature port’s price (9)

blocks.note: ground = rubbed together, as teeth are

annotation.surface: Someone scrapes together the cost of a vintage port.
annotation.walkthrough: The port is a harbour, not the drink the surface pours.
annotation.definitionFit: Groundage is the fee a ship pays to lie in a port.

entries.clue: Policeman arrests disorderly Baltimore suspect (11)

indicatorNotes.arrests: PC holds the next piece inside
indicatorNotes.disorderly: the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: A cop collars a rowdy suspect in Baltimore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' is the adjective, not the person being arrested.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: a suspect claim is open to doubt, which is what a problematic one is.

entries.clue: Recently abroad with a touring Italian in Rome (7,4)

indicatorNotes.touring: the letters travel around into a new order

blocks.note: It = Italian, as in gin and It

annotation.surface: A traveller just back from a trip with an Italian in Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: Rome has been called the Eternal City since antiquity.
annotation.definitionFit: The Eternal City is Rome's ancient nickname.

entries.clue: Primate and bishop, reflecting regularly, doubt own God (6)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: the letters come back as in a mirror
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, like a steady beat, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: dOuBt OwN gOd gives OBONO, reversed

annotation.surface: An archbishop and a bishop, on reflection, now and then doubt their own God.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primate' plus 'bishop' paints a Church picture; the primate is an ape.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this ape from the Congo belongs to the order of primates, alongside us.

entries.clue: Track flying bird, returning record penned by left hand (6,4)

indicatorNotes.flying: the letters of BIRD fly into a new order
indicatorNotes.returning: TAPE goes back the other way
indicatorNotes.penned by: L and H enclose the reversed record

annotation.surface: Someone tracks a bird in flight, then writes the record down left-handed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left hand' reads as one thing; it splits into L and H, which hold the record between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A bridle path is a track meant for riders on horseback.

entries.clue: A worker on ship caught violent attacker (8)

indicatorNotes.caught: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so the words are to be heard, not read

blocks.note: a sailor works on a ship

annotation.surface: A deckhand was arrested for assault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' reads as an arrest; it means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: Formed from the verb: to assail is to set upon violently, so the one doing it is the attacker.

entries.clue: Notice about bank limits not for writing on (4-4)

indicatorNotes.limits: RELY bounds the other pieces on both sides

blocks.note: on = about, as in a talk on birds

annotation.surface: A bank puts up a sign about its withdrawal limits that customers must not deface.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb, as in 'you can bank on it'.
annotation.definitionFit: A read-only file or disk can be read but not written to.

entries.clue: Arouse Earl on leave, bored by Charlie (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, E goes after EXIT
indicatorNotes.bored by: 'bored' in its drilling sense, so C tunnels into the middle of the word

blocks.note: Charlie = C in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An earl on holiday finds himself bored by a friend called Charlie.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer arouses; the surface is a man bored stiff.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, verb for verb: news that excites a crowd arouses it.

entries.clue: Dialogue from The Lovers, possibly — a Debra Winger film (5,2,10)

blocks.note: lovers call each other darling, sweetheart and so on
the 1983 film starring Debra Winger and Shirley MacLaine

annotation.surface: A line from a film called The Lovers, compared with a Debra Winger picture.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'The Lovers' look like a film title, matching the second half; it is just lovers in general.
annotation.definitionFit: Lovers' pet names are terms of endearment, and that is also the title of Winger's 1983 film.

entries.clue: Behave theatrically after reading, maybe, and faint (6)

blocks.note: reading is one of the three Rs

annotation.surface: An actor hams it up after a script reading and then swoons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' puts EMOTE after R. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R can stand for reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective in the sense of slight: a faint hope and a remote possibility are equally unlikely.

entries.clue: Introductory item on screen going into quarry (10)

indicatorNotes.going into: going into a place means ending up inside it, so the screen item sits inside the quarry

blocks.note: the cursor on a computer screen

annotation.surface: An opening shot appears on screen as the hunt closes in on its quarry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' is the hunted animal, not a pit.
annotation.definitionFit: Built from precursor, a forerunner: something precursory comes first and leads into what follows.

entries.clue: Inside joke overheard by journalist and absorbed (8)

indicatorNotes.overheard: use the sound of the word

annotation.surface: A journalist overhears an in-joke and is gripped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside joke' reads as an in-joke; it splits into IN and the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Past tense for past tense: food ingested is swallowed and taken into the body, as a sponge absorbs water.

entries.clue: One flagging in role as public representative? (8-6)

annotation.definition: One flagging in role as public representative?

blocks.note: the surface reads a person wilting; the setter means a person carrying a flag, or standard
the figurative sense: the leading public face of a cause or party

annotation.surface: A spokesperson is tiring in the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flagging' means wilting in the surface; here it means carrying a flag, the standard.
annotation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer carries a flag, and is the public face of a movement.

entries.clue: Criticise medic spreading infectious disease (8)

indicatorNotes.spreading: MEDIC's letters spread out into a new order

annotation.surface: A doctor is blamed for spreading an infection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' belongs with the disease in the surface; it is working on 'medic'.
annotation.definitionFit: A pandemic is an infectious disease spread across the world.

entries.clue: Head cut from Melania Trump’s plant (5)

indicatorNotes.Head cut from: a word's head is its first letter, and cutting it off leaves the rest

blocks.note: FLOTUS, First Lady of the United States, without its F

annotation.surface: Melania Trump's houseplant has been pruned.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is possessive in the surface but 'is' in the wordplay. FLOTUS is the White House acronym for the First Lady.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this water lily, sacred in Asia, is a plant.

entries.clue: Professor at Oregon entertains accomplished speaker (6)

indicatorNotes.entertains: the phrase holds the answer inside it

annotation.surface: An Oregon professor hosts a noted lecturer.
annotation.walkthrough: The academic setting fits the answer, which is why the hidden word slips past.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is reserved for speakers with polish, like Cicero, hence 'accomplished'.

entries.clue: Variety of tunes spun on radio touches Greek character so (5,5)

indicatorNotes.on radio: broadcast, so heard rather than seen

blocks.note: sic = thus, so, marking a quoted error

annotation.surface: A DJ plays an assortment of tracks and also touches on a Greek figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spun on radio' looks like records being played; it is the sound of 'whirled'.
annotation.definitionFit: World music is a broad genre of international popular and folk music.

entries.clue: With first half upset, flair not visible (6)

indicatorNotes.With first half upset: turn only the first three letters upside down

annotation.surface: Someone's gift stays hidden once they are knocked off balance.
annotation.walkthrough: Only TAL is reversed; ENT stays put.
annotation.definitionFit: Latent means present but not yet visible.

entries.clue: Their captors arranged sunken area to play in (9,3)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters are put in a new order, as music is arranged

annotation.surface: Kidnappers set up a hidden pit for their hostages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' carries its musical sense in disguise, fitting the orchestra.
annotation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit is the lowered area in front of a stage where the musicians play.

entries.clue: Separated writers author sitcom (3,7)

annotation.surface: Estranged scriptwriters create a sitcom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Separated' suggests a split; pen friends are simply far apart, writing letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Pen friends write to each other across a distance.

entries.clue: Achieve great success as one in tower might? (4,3,4)

blocks.note: from the fairground test of strength
a bell-ringer in a church tower

annotation.surface: A bell-ringer hits the big time.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second half.
annotation.definitionFit: To ring the bell is to score a hit, as at a fairground strength machine.

entries.clue: Identifying band as “rap metal” originally permitted (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: A music group is labelled rap metal and allowed to perform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' is a group of musicians in the surface; it is a strip worn on the arm.
annotation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn round the arm, often for identification.

entries.clue: Such a long way to this point (2,3)

blocks.note: the distance sense: 'I've come this great a distance'
the time sense: up until now

annotation.surface: Someone remarks on how far they have come.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are plain senses of the phrase, one of distance and one of time.
annotation.definitionFit: So far means both to such a distance and up to now.

entries.clue: Honest Frenchman shortly to be in French area (6,5)

annotation.surface: A decent Frenchman is soon to be in some region of France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French area' looks like the definition; only 'area' is, and 'to be in French' is ETRE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a square one metre on each side is a standard metric measure of area.

entries.clue: Posters in church facility lining sides of building (10)

indicatorNotes.lining: WALLS line the other pieces on both sides

blocks.note: a building's walls are its sides

annotation.surface: Posters are put up in a church hall lining its walls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' sounds like a building; it is a knack or skill.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: large printed sheets pinned up in classrooms, such as the periodic table, are posters.

entries.clue: Shy PA may attend dances for emotional support (3,3,8)

indicatorNotes.dances: the letters move about into a new order

annotation.surface: A timid assistant might go to dances to be comforted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dances' looks like what the PA attends; it is the anagram signal, and 'may attend' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Tea and sympathy is British for kindly comfort offered to someone upset.

entries.clue: Reserve covering kid’s small period of absence (4,5)

indicatorNotes.covering: a covering wraps round what it covers, so the reserve word goes outside the small one

blocks.note: ickle is baby talk for little

annotation.surface: A parent keeps a spare for their child's short time off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid's small' is a word a child would say: ickle, British baby talk for little.
annotation.definitionFit: Sick leave is time off work through illness.

entries.clue: Bar open, welcoming heroine at last … Pussy Galore? (8)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: a host welcoming a guest takes them inside, so the open word takes the letter in
indicatorNotes.at last: 'at last' means at the very end, so only the word's final letter is used

annotation.surface: A bar opens its doors to a Bond heroine.
annotation.walkthrough: Pussy Galore, the Goldfinger character, is a famous double entendre; the question mark says she is an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the Bond girl's name is a famous double meaning.

entries.clue: Axe vital works? This should make going easier (8)

indicatorNotes.works: the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: Cutting essential public works would supposedly help traffic flow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going' is lavatorial; 'works' is the anagram signal, not factories.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description rather than a synonym: 'going' is the euphemism for a bowel movement, which a laxative eases.

entries.clue: Mention husband harbouring crabs initially comes over feverish (6)

indicatorNotes.harbouring: a harbour shelters ships inside it, so the mention-and-husband word shelters the letter
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of 'crabs' is used
indicatorNotes.comes over: to come over is to turn across, so the whole thing flips and reads backwards

annotation.surface: A wife mentions that her husband has crabs, and she comes over all feverish.
annotation.walkthrough: CITE+H with C inside gives CITCEH, and that flipped is the answer. Hectic once meant feverish, as in a hectic flush.
annotation.definitionFit: Hectic originally meant feverish, as in a hectic fever.

entries.clue: Massive fuel deficit spreads (8)

indicatorNotes.spreads: to spread is to stretch out, so the fuel word stretches to reach round the deficit

annotation.surface: A huge fuel shortage is widening.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a news headline about a fuel crisis, so 'spreads' looks like the shortage growing rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Colossus of Rhodes: anything colossal is massive in size.

entries.clue: Fearful look around entering outskirts of Coventry (6)

indicatorNotes.around: to look around is to turn round, so the look word is turned back to front
indicatorNotes.entering: entering a place puts you inside it, so the turned look goes between the edge letters
indicatorNotes.outskirts of: a town's outskirts are its edges, so only the first and last letters of Coventry are used

annotation.surface: A nervous person looks about on the edge of Coventry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fearful' here means causing fear, the older sense, not feeling it.
annotation.definitionFit: Fearful in the sense of frightening is what creepy means.

entries.clue: Support for Jimmy White drops again after rising (6)

indicatorNotes.after rising: in a down clue, read the word upward

annotation.surface: A backer of the snooker star Jimmy White falls away again after a surge.
annotation.walkthrough: Jimmy White is an English snooker player, and a spider is the raised rest a snooker player props the cue on.
annotation.definitionFit: The spider is a snooker rest, a support for a cue.

entries.clue: Abraham’s wife retired with small dog (6)

blocks.note: Sarah, wife of Abraham in Genesis, reversed

annotation.surface: An old woman goes to bed with a little pet dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb: to dog someone is to pester them.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb for verb: to dog someone is to follow and pester them, as a dog hounds its quarry.

entries.clue: Pre-prepared food was underwhelming for Spooner (6,5)

indicatorNotes.for Spooner: swap the opening sounds, as Dr Spooner did

blocks.note: something underwhelming lacked punch, had no impact
swap the L and P sounds

annotation.surface: A ready meal proved a letdown.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the L of 'lacked' and the P of 'punch'.
annotation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food prepared in advance to eat later.

entries.clue: Easy way to serve peas if starter becomes cold (5)

indicatorNotes.if starter becomes: change the first letter into another

blocks.note: mushy peas, a British side dish of mashed peas

annotation.surface: A simple way to dish up peas, served cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course beside the peas; it is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British synonym, from army slang: a comfortable, undemanding posting is an easy number.

entries.clue: DEA agent’s informant really vocal (5)

indicatorNotes.vocal: vocal means using the voice, so the words are to be spoken aloud and matched by sound

blocks.note: a nark is an informer; 'oh!' = really?

annotation.surface: A drugs agent's snitch turns out to be very talkative.
annotation.walkthrough: The DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration; narco is American slang for a narcotics agent. Nark is British slang for an informer.
annotation.definitionFit: A narco is a narcotics agent, such as one working for the DEA.

entries.clue: Criminal lair trademark exposed officer (4,7)

indicatorNotes.Criminal: the letters are crooked, out of order

blocks.note: TRADEMARK without its outer T and K

annotation.surface: A criminal's hideout reveals the brand mark of a police officer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' means stripped of its covering, the first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the rank just below vice admiral is a senior naval officer.

entries.clue: Author to enter cabin (5)

blocks.note: a specific writer: the English novelist David, author of Nice Work
a small hut, as on a ski slope or at an estate gate

annotation.surface: A writer goes into a hut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To enter' is a third sense: to lodge something, such as an appeal, is to enter it formally.
annotation.definitionFit: David Lodge is a novelist, and a lodge is a small cabin.

entries.clue: Desperate couple accepting society’s state of collapse (9)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept something is to take it in, so the desperate word takes the letter into itself

annotation.surface: A couple at the end of their tether accept society's breakdown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desperate couple' reads as one pair of people; it is DIRE then PAIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun for noun: a building fallen into disrepair is crumbling, in a state of collapse.

entries.clue: Model salesperson, left in charge, leads area (7)

indicatorNotes.leads: the earlier pieces go before A

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative

annotation.surface: A model saleswoman, left in charge, heads up a region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' is the noun for a copy, not a fashion model.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun for noun: a scale model of a ship or car is a replica, an exact copy of the original.

entries.clue: Beginning to tailor tiny Scottish duke’s cloth for suits (5)

indicatorNotes.Beginning to: take the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: A tailor starts on a small Scottish duke's suiting fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scottish setting is apt: tweed is woven in Scotland, and the River Tweed runs along its border.
annotation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth for suits and jackets.

entries.clue: In Windsor, I would firstly set about cracking eggs (5,2)

annotation.definitionNote: the royal we is what a Windsor says in place of 'I'

indicatorNotes.firstly: firstly means before anything else, so only the opening letter of 'would' is used
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'about turn', so the letters face the other way
indicatorNotes.cracking: cracking an egg breaks into it, so the reversed letters go inside the eggs

annotation.surface: At Windsor, someone would set about cracking eggs for breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: The Windsors are the British royal family, and a monarch speaking of themself traditionally says 'we' for 'I'.
annotation.definitionFit: The royal we is the 'we' a monarch uses for 'I'.

entries.clue: Possible location of film actor’s birth (5)

blocks.note: where an actor is during filming, in two words
birth in its figurative sense: a beginning, as of a disease or winter

annotation.surface: A film star's birthplace is being discussed.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration (5) runs 'on set' together into one word.
annotation.definitionFit: Two readings of one string: split, it is where an actor works; joined, it is the start of something, its birth.

entries.clue: Cover sheet manufactured with an unfinished hem (9)

indicatorNotes.manufactured: the letters are made into something new
indicatorNotes.unfinished: an unfinished job stops short of the end, so the word loses its final letter

annotation.surface: A cover sheet is made with a hem left incomplete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover sheet' reads as a noun phrase; 'cover' is the verb definition, 'sheet' the start of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb for verb: to put a blade in its sheath is to cover it, and the word widens to any enclosing cover.
